Company relationships/Source notes

Data provenance and method

This page documents the dataset and transformations used by the company relationship explorer. The research snapshot was exported on October 20, 2026; the article and interface were redesigned on November 9, 2026.

The historical graph

The export contains 477 companies: the 475-company research universe plus SkyWest and Republic, two historical counterparties needed by the filing pilot. It contains 36,111 unique typed relationships derived from 67,184 original typed rows. It is not a complete supplier database. Profile assertions, filing candidates, and reviewed filing links remain distinct.

  • stock_graph/profiles_ext.py: company descriptions and shared economic drivers. Profiles were reconstructed retrospectively and intended to describe 2010-era structure.
  • stock_graph/results/options_graph_5y/analysis_edges.csv: relationship types, supplier/customer direction, economic explanations, and historical-change flags.
  • stock_graph/results/filing_relationships/candidates.csv: Apple/Intel filing candidates and dated source references.
  • stock_graph/results/filing_relationships/reviewed_edges.csv: reviewed parent-level SkyWest/Delta and Republic/Delta links through regional-carrier subsidiaries.
  • stock_graph/docs/FILING_RELATIONSHIP_PILOT.md: review decisions, rule-development sample, and validation limits.

These paths identify the original workspace records; they are not hosted routes. The website serves the static JSON export, which includes source references for the filing-backed records. It does not include licensed price panels or option quotes.

From research rows to browser links

Supply links are stored once, from supplier to customer; their reverse SUPPLY_DOWN rows are omitted. Competitor, shared-driver and dual-class links are deduplicated as symmetric pairs. Input-cost directions are retained. Existing filing-pilot evidence overlays the Intel/Apple link and adds the two Delta counterparties. No price or options panel is published.

The default shows named profile assertions and filing records. “Include inferred candidates” adds links generated from overlapping business tags. Neither a named profile nor an inferred tag match establishes a verified contract. All 477 companies remain visible in the unfiltered overview, including those without links under the active filters.

This is a static historical snapshot, interactive in the browser. It is not a real-time feed and does not automatically update company relationships.

Tracing a scenario

Supply arrows run from supplier to customer. A demand scenario follows those links backward; a supply-disruption scenario follows them forward. An unweighted breadth-first search returns companies reachable within one or two hops, counting each company once at its shortest distance.

Only supply links transmit these scenarios. Competitor, shared-driver, and input-cost links can be inspected as context. The evidence, relationship-basis, sector and relationship-type filters apply before the trace. Neighborhood mode shows the focal company, its direct neighbors, and any additional companies reached by a trace.

The algorithm identifies paths, not effects. It uses no estimated coefficients, contract weights, probabilities, causal signs, or expected returns. The overview groups companies by sector; neighborhood mode uses a deterministic spiral around the focal company. Locations are display choices, not estimates. Equal node sizes do not imply equal business exposure.

Reading the evidence

A profile assertion has not been independently established by the attached filing pilot. An Intel component mention in an Apple filing remains a candidate for a direct purchasing link. The reviewed Delta links are parent-level interpretations based on named subsidiaries, not observations of current contracts.

A disclosure date is not the contract’s start date. Missing end dates do not establish continuing validity. The small filing pilot was used to design its extraction rules, so review on that sample does not establish performance on unseen firms.

Typography and hosting

Roboto and Libre Baskerville are bundled locally with their SIL Open Font License texts under assets/fonts/. There are no remote font, analytics or application API calls. The graph runs directly in the browser; downloads are optional.

Run or publish

The complete website is the dist/ directory. It runs on a static HTTP server with no dependencies or build step:

python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory dist

The source download includes a GitHub Pages workflow. Configure Pages to use GitHub Actions and push the project to a repository whose default branch is main. The workflow checks the local sources and publishes dist/. Repository subpaths work because application assets and data URLs are relative.
